readings: Join Invoices to Orders and Customers, keeping only rows that link through all three tables. For each distinct Customers.gender value, count distinct Orders.order_id values that have at least one invoice. Divide each count by the total number of distinct invoiced orders to get its share. Compute the arithmetic mean of those gender shares, then return only genders whose share exceeds that mean, with the gender, order count, unrounded share, and unrounded difference from the mean.

Join Invoices to Orders and Customers, keeping only rows that link through all three tables. For each distinct Customers.gender value, count invoice–order matches, counting an order again for each additional invoice. Divide each count by the total number of invoice–order matches to get its share. Compute the arithmetic mean of those gender shares, then return only genders whose share exceeds that mean, with the gender, match count, unrounded share, and unrounded difference from the mean.
queries:
WITH invoiced_orders AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT c.gender, o.order_id
    FROM Invoices AS i
    JOIN Orders AS o ON o.order_id = i.order_id
    JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
),
gender_counts AS (
    SELECT gender, COUNT(*) AS order_count
    FROM invoiced_orders
    GROUP BY gender
),
gender_shares AS (
    SELECT gender,
           order_count,
           1.0 * order_count / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM invoiced_orders) AS share
    FROM gender_counts
)
SELECT gender,
       order_count,
       share,
       share - (SELECT AVG(share) FROM gender_shares) AS difference_from_mean
FROM gender_shares
WHERE share > (SELECT AVG(share) FROM gender_shares);

WITH gender_counts AS (
    SELECT c.gender, COUNT(*) AS match_count
    FROM Invoices AS i
    JOIN Orders AS o ON o.order_id = i.order_id
    JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    GROUP BY c.gender
),
gender_shares AS (
    SELECT gender,
           match_count,
           match_count * 1.0 / SUM(match_count) OVER () AS share
    FROM gender_counts
)
SELECT gender,
       match_count,
       share,
       share - (SELECT AVG(share) FROM gender_shares) AS difference_from_mean
FROM gender_shares
WHERE share > (SELECT AVG(share) FROM gender_shares)
